title: Proof-carrying enforcement, collision isolation, and safe post-merge cleanup
summary: Preserve the landed v2.17.11 ReviewKernel fixes, then add one exact-workspace enforcement decision, one versioned collision/interference authority, and one durable two-phase merge/cleanup transaction that removes only revalidated Taskplane-managed linked worktrees.

current_state.summary: v2.17.11 already normalizes derivable ReviewKernel summaries, retries substantive slot changes narrowly, preserves provenance/conservation, treats evaluator outages as unavailable, renders all contract shapes, resolves live review manifests, supports Python 3.10-3.12, and binds evaluation to claimed worktrees. Remaining gaps are advisory-only Claude liveness, opt-in dispatch screening with no Skill matcher or collision registry, no signed-root exclusion/interference ledger, and merge/removal prose without a durable merge receipt or conservative cleanup owner.

alternatives.name: Canonical proof records with two-phase cleanup
alternatives.description: Add kernel-owned enforcement, collision/interference, and cleanup decisions; adapters consume them, and cleanup starts only after a durable orchestrator merge receipt and immediate eligibility revalidation.

gains: One cross-host authority truth and evidence id
Structural collision denial without prose dependence
costs: Three focused Python modules and one packaged registry
State-machine, crash, Git, and host-parity fixture matrices
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Hosts expose an authenticated repository-scoped enforcement and plugin-exclusion protocol with equivalent receipts, audit, and cleanup transaction semantics.

alternatives.name: Distributed adapter checks and immediate removal
alternatives.description: Implement liveness and collision checks independently in hooks, CLI, status, and dashboard, then have the merge driver remove a worktree immediately after Git succeeds.

gains: Small local patches at each surface
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Taskplane supports only one host, one entry surface, and one non-parallel repository layout.

alternatives.name: Status quo warnings and manual cleanup
alternatives.description: Keep liveness advisory, rely on users to disable competing plugins, and leave worktree removal to the orchestrator or human.

costs: Competing delivery loops remain structurally allowed
Merged managed worktrees continue to accumulate
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Used only as explicit warn/manual rollback mode after canonical records exist.

decision: Select canonical proof records because R-0003 requires identical structural classifications across surfaces and requires cleanup to be both destructive and crash-safe. A single decision per concern, persisted with existing atomic run-store primitives and projected by adapters, is the smallest design that makes those invariants mechanically reviewable.

acceptance_map.validation: Run `python3 -m pytest -q taskplane/tests/test_review_evidence_lifecycle.py -k 'metadata_contradiction or normalizes_derivable or canonical_result'`; assert one repair audit, unchanged finding bytes, complete collection, and no producer rerun.

acceptance_map.validation: Run `python3 -m pytest -q taskplane/tests/test_review_evidence_lifecycle.py -k 'substantive_mutation or fail_to_pass'`; assert one affected slot, max-attempt bound, sealed sibling reuse, and original run/slot lineage.

risks.risk: A legitimate Claude session is locked out by missing or stale structural proof.
risks.mitigation: Use the entry call's own fresh receipt, exact 300-second fallback only when session identity is unknown, host-specific recovery, attributable advisory, and warn mode as rollback without forging live.

risks.risk: Collision rules falsely deny a helper or classify a directory by name.
risks.mitigation: Use a versioned fingerprinted registry, explicit helper patterns, signed multi-file state layouts, exact governed-state checks, advised unknowns by default, and fixture corpus for both false-positive directions.

risks.risk: Cleanup destroys unmerged bytes or targets a foreign/path-swapped tree.
risks.mitigation: Require exact managed registration and recorded identities, lstat non-link checks, clean porcelain-v2 bytes, lifecycle/variant/retention checks, local ancestry, and an immediate second read under lock before one no-force exact-path call.

risks.risk: A crash splits Git removal from the cleanup outcome record.
risks.mitigation: Persist merge first, key cleanup by receipt, verify path and registration after removal, and permit one exact already-clean maintenance replay; partial absence becomes manual-attention.

risks.risk: Removing a worker checkout makes review or sign-off evidence unreachable.
risks.mitigation: Require canonical external evidence before lifecycle release, preserve evidence-needed trees, retain all branches/commits/run records, and run EM-through-sign-off after-removal fixtures.

risks.risk: New Python modules or packaged registry break supported interpreters/installations.
risks.mitigation: Use synchronous stdlib-only Python 3.10 syntax, runtime-validate trust boundaries, include the JSON resource in wheel/plugin contents, and run clean-wheel imports plus 3.10/3.11/3.12 smoke jobs.

failure_modes.mode: Strict entry or closure cannot prove a live screen.
failure_modes.detection: enforcement_gate_refused signal contains status, evidence_id, host, surface, and recovery.
failure_modes.recovery: The human reloads/retries for fresh proof or records one `--advisory --by` decision; no automatic retry or partial state creation occurs.

failure_modes.mode: A known competing driver or unknown strict-isolation invocation is attempted.
failure_modes.detection: foreign_interference_event signal contains registry fingerprint, disposition, run, step, identity, and continuation.
failure_modes.recovery: The hook denies once and directs the orchestrator to the exact Taskplane continuation; advisory observations remain non-denial records.

failure_modes.mode: Foreign-state signature discovery is unreadable or ambiguous.
failure_modes.detection: foreign_state_detected signal records only proven roots; a bounded discovery diagnostic records uncertainty without naming an unsigned root.
failure_modes.recovery: Contract compilation fails closed for the uncertain candidate root or requires an attributable exact-root override; status reads the last durable result.

failure_modes.mode: Merge succeeds but the durable merge receipt is not committed.
failure_modes.detection: merge_recorded signal is absent while the task worktree registration remains present.
failure_modes.recovery: No cleanup runs; the orchestrator re-resolves the merge state and explicitly records it or preserves the tree for manual attention.

failure_modes.mode: Eligibility changes between merge and cleanup or at last-moment revalidation.
failure_modes.detection: worktree_cleanup_preserved signal names the exact failed invariant and unchanged candidate identity.
failure_modes.recovery: The cleanup owner performs no removal; only a later state change plus one bounded maintenance pass may reconsider the same registered candidate.

failure_modes.mode: Git removal fails or leaves path/registration state inconsistent.
failure_modes.detection: worktree_cleanup_manual_attention signal contains exit class and postcondition state without command output secrets.
failure_modes.recovery: Stop permanently for that outcome fingerprint; never force, broaden, delete a branch, or retry automatically. A human resolves the exact Git condition.

failure_modes.mode: The process crashes after exact removal but before outcome persistence.
failure_modes.detection: worktree_cleanup_already_clean signal is produced when one replay sees the same durable receipt and both exact path and exact registration absent.
failure_modes.recovery: The maintenance owner commits already-clean once and performs no Git mutation.

signals: enforcement_decision: stable status/evidence_id with exact workspace, session, run, revision, and optional advisory attribution
enforcement_gate_refused: strict entry/closure surface, reason, evidence_id, and host recovery
foreign_interference_event: bounded identity, disposition, registry fingerprint, governed run/step, and time
foreign_state_detected: signed root, signature id/version, exclusion or attributable override
merge_recorded: durable receipt id, repository/task/branch tip, primary ref/tip, and time
worktree_cleanup_preserved: receipt id, failed invariant, exact candidate, and no-mutation outcome
worktree_cleanup_removed: receipt id plus verified path/registration absence
worktree_cleanup_already_clean: replay id and exact absent postconditions
worktree_cleanup_manual_attention: receipt id, bounded failure class, and inconsistent postcondition
alerts: Dashboard and machine output surface every strict enforcement refusal with one host-specific recovery.
Known collision denials name the run, step, identity, and exact Taskplane continuation.
Cleanup manual-attention is a status/retro headline and disables further automatic attempts for the same outcome fingerprint.

rollout.strategy: Land and pin v2.17.11 ReviewKernel regression floors first; add versioned record schemas and read-only projections; wire exact receipt trust and strict Claude entry/closure; add Skill/dispatch collision screening with known conflicts denied and unknowns advised; add signed-root exclusion; then introduce the orchestrator merge receipt and enable automatic cleanup only after the full preservation/crash matrix passes. Keep all changes additive and stdlib-only.
rollout.rollback: Set enforcement to warn, disable collision screening, and set cleanup to manual while retaining truthful unproven/advisory status, all audit/merge/cleanup records, and every ReviewKernel floor. Rollback cannot auto-approve, claim live without proof, delete branches/evidence, or invoke force removal.

visualization.reason: The enforcement, collision, and cleanup state machines plus the durable merge-before-remove sequence contain multiple fail-closed branches that are materially clearer together.

lens_evidence.evidence: Applied hash-verified Python guidance; checked the proposal against v2.17.11 review, receipt, contract, loop, storage, run-store, dashboard, hook, and test seams; compared three materially different approaches; mapped all 28 exact criteria to runnable fixtures; tied every failure detection to a declared signal; made rollback additive and conservative; and surfaced Python 3.10-3.12 packaging, synchronous ownership, trust-boundary validation, RPO 0 after reported commits, one-pass cleanup RTO, 300-second receipt freshness, zero entry probes, and p95 <=100 ms local hook bounds.
